**Objectives of the Tutorial/Lab**
By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

- Simulate data from finite Poisson mixture models.
- Derive the E-step and M-step of the EM algorithm for a Poisson mixture.
- Implement and interpret the EM algorithm for a Poisson mixture model.

## Question 1

Simulate 100 samples from the following mixture model. For $i=1, \ldots, 100$,
$$
Z_i \sim \text{categorical }(0.8, 0.2),
$$

$$
X_i | Z_i = 1 \sim \text{Pois}(\lambda_1=2) \text{ and } X_i | Z_i = 2 \sim \text{Pois}(\lambda_2=8).
$$

The Poisson distribution has probability mass function

$$
f(x; \lambda) = \frac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x!}.
$$

Please set a seed using `set.seed(30027)`. Make a histogram of the simulated samples.

## Question 2

We pretend that we just observe the simulated samples. We will assume that the observed data follow a mixture of two Poisson distributions. Specifically, for $i=1, \ldots, 100$,
$$
Z_i \sim \text{categorical }(\pi_1, 1-\pi_1),
$$

$$
X_i | Z_i = 1 \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_1) \text{ and } X_i | Z_i = 2 \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_2).
$$

We aim to obtain MLE of parameters $\theta = (\pi_1, \lambda_1, \lambda_2)$ using the EM algorithm.
